extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients (program directors/principal investigators, signing officials, and administrative staff who submit RPPRs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and electronically submitting the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) variations (Annual, Interim, Final) for NIH grants via eRA Commons, including roles, timing, and required content elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory electronic submission via RPPR module
rubrics_metrics.description: All progress reports for NIH grants must be submitted electronically using the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) module in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Grants & Funding’s RPPR webpage for details. You must be logged into eRA Commons with appropriate role(s) to complete these activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual RPPR content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual RPPR — Used to describe a grant’s scientific progress, identify significant changes, report on personnel, and describe plans for the subsequent budget period or year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Annual RPPR form and navigation tabs in the RPPR module (screenshots provided). Include descriptions of scientific progress, personnel changes, significant changes, and plans for the upcoming budget period/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR purpose and equivalence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim RPPR — Used when submitting a renewal (Type 2) application. If the Type 2 is not funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the Final RPPR for the project. If the Type 2 is funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the annual RPPR for the final year of the previous competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data elements collected on the Interim RPPR are the same as for the Final RPPR, including project outcomes. Submit Interim RPPR no later than 120 days from the project period end date when submitting a competing renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR purpose at closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Final RPPR — Used as part of the grant closeout process to submit project outcomes in addition to the information submitted on the annual RPPR, except budget and plans for the upcoming year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit Final RPPR no later than 120 days from the project period end date when not submitting a competing renewal. Final RPPR focuses on project outcomes and closeout reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR submission deadlines relative to project period end date
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit Final RPPR no later than 120 days from the project period end date. Submit Interim RPPR no later than 120 days from the project period end date when submitting a competing renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Competing Renewal Application Status scenarios: Not submitting a Competing Renewal application → submit Final RPPR; Submitting a Competing Renewal application → submit Interim RPPR. Be aware of the acceptance rules if the renewal is funded or not funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities for initiating and submitting RPPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: For Program Directors/Principal Investigators to initiate an RPPR; For Signing Officials to submit an RPPR in eRA Commons; For Signing Officials to delegate submission of an RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PI/PD initiates the RPPR; a Signing Official (SO) accesses and submits via the Status module (three-dot ellipsis menu) or can delegate submission. You must be logged into eRA Commons with appropriate role(s). See 'RPPR: Who Can Do What?' and 'eRA Commons Roles & Privileges At a Glance' for role-specific privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress reports must document accomplishments and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports document the recipient’s accomplishments and compliance with terms of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the RPPR content demonstrates scientific accomplishments and addresses compliance matters required by the award terms and NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reminder: Reporting Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan Activities in RPPRs Submitted on or after October 1, 2024 (NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-24-175).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For RPPRs submitted on/after Oct 1, 2024, include reporting on DMS plan activities as required by the referenced Guide Notice. Consult the policy link for details on what to report and how to document DMS activities in the RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NIH policy and program-specific RPPR implementations
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPR submissions must follow the NIH Grants Policy Statement requirements for RPPR and Final Progress Report and any program-specific implementation notices (e.g., SBIR/STTR implementations, changes to biosketch and Other Support format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult relevant NIH Guide Notices (e.g., NOT-OD-17-085, NOT-OD-17-037, NOT-OD-17-022, NOT-OD-21-110) and the NIH Grants Policy Statement: RPPR and Final Progress Report for program-specific rules and formatting requirements.
